trad music. A good way to get to know Irish culture
talk to old Irish people about Irish history. Young people are a lot more detahced from that.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
travel travel travel. Ireland is such a beautiful country, and the whole west coast is just incredible.
If you like surfing, get a wet suit and you'll have some of the best surfing in Europe. If you like hiking there are tons of hikes.
Go to small towns and seek out locals in the pubs, learn about the history of one of the only countries in Europe that was colonised up until the 20 th century.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I am Irhs so for eme it was easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: just do it. sport is a good way

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: none, except that everything closes very early compared to Denmark

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the openness, welcoming nature of Irish people. and the story telling and music

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
bring loads of money.
dont get scammed with housing.
please dont spend the whole semster stuck insdie the campus library. it is a bit hard to travel around without a car, but well worth it. please go and find the most hidden obscure pubs, talk to locals, learn about colonial history, Irish mythology, and learn to enjoy the dosens of different types of rain the country had to offer

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: talking to older Irish people, learning about Ireland through my course in Irish cinema and aesthetics, and having loads of pints of beer, even though theu're expensive.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: the housing, the lack of sun, and the fact that the nightlife closed so early.
